title: Retry, then escalate, a model-switch Stop that fails
prompt:
GitHub issue #3: https://github.com/acupof-ai/Spawn/issues/3. Read it, then `delivery()`, `orders()`, `attempts()` and `news_items()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs, `decide_with()` and `step()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs, and crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch/digest.rs.

The problem. When a task needs the other model profile than the one its live worker runs on, `delivery()` stops the worker first with a Stop under the fixed key `switch-model-<task>-<revision>`; once the worker is down, a later pass resumes it on the task's profile with the task. When that Stop fails (state finished, succeeded false), the worker stays live on the wrong profile and the task stays `assigned`. Every later pass plans the same Stop under the same key, which `spawn_submit` deduplicates to the old finished command, so nothing runs again. No escalation is raised either. The task waits forever with no signal to anyone.

What the issue says that no longer holds at this commit (line numbers have moved too): a task is no longer marked delivered when its command is submitted. `decide_with()` marks it delivered once its delivery command has succeeded (`Plan::delivered`). A failed delivery (`deliver-<task>-<revision>`) is already retried under `<key>-retry-<n>` (3 retries, a wait of 60 s doubling to 30 min) and then escalated as `DeliveryFailed` for a waiting (assigned or revise) task, not only a delivered one. The switch Stop is outside that machinery: it is not a delivery attempt, so nothing tracks its failures. The rest of the issue holds: the same-key replanning, the dedup, no escalation, and the worker ladder skipping a managed session whose task is not in flight.

A trap the issue does not mention: after a failed Stop, the worker's latest judgement goes stale. An Observer with no model judge writes a new judgement only when it changes, and the Stop's own records are newer than it, so `Facts::idle_at_prompt()` turns false and stays false while the worker sits idle. A failed Stop changed nothing on the worker. A retry that waits for a fresh idle judgement of it never comes.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks):
1. After a switch Stop fails, the task stays waiting, and the dispatcher submits another Stop to the same session under a new idempotency key once a retry is due. A retry is due at most one hour after the failure.
2. After at most 5 Stops in all for one task revision, it stops retrying: no further Stop for that task.
3. It then escalates to the supervisor. A digest (an Input from `spawn-dispatch` into `session_supervisor`) carries an escalation whose tag is `<the worker's session id> <id>`, other than the resident's approval item, and whose line names the task as `task #<id>`. A `DeliveryFailed` escalation saying the worker could not be stopped to switch its model fits.
4. The task is never marked delivered by any of this, and stays `assigned`.
Retrying like a failed delivery (keys `switch-model-<task>-<revision>-retry-<n>`, the same backoff and count, then a `DeliveryFailed` escalation) satisfies this. Add unit tests in deliver.rs next to the existing switch tests: a failed switch Stop retried under a new key only once due, no Stop after the last retry, the escalation, and a switch Stop that succeeds still leading to the Resume that delivers.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/006.sh (read it). A resident `core` runs live on the default profile, idle at its prompt, under `spawn loop` with a fake engine and no model judge. A task on the cheap profile is assigned to it. Its terminal refuses to be killed (a tmux wrapper fails `kill-session`), so every Stop of it fails. The scenario ages each failed Stop by two hours, so any retry wait of up to an hour is over. It keeps the supervisor's judgement fresh by typing a line into it now and then, but leaves the worker alone. It requires a retry under a new key, at most 5 Stops, the digest described above within 240 s, no Stop after the escalation, and the task still `assigned`. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
